items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: we made a film called the Big Broadcast of 1935 with Amos and Andy

ctx.x: Which I would like to get into later on, and we made a film called the Big Broadcast of 1935 with Amos and Andy, but we made our part of it, not in Hollywood, but I think Astoria, New York, and we were playing at that time at the Rainbow Room till 3:00 in the morning and then we'd get in bed at 4 or 5 and we had to be on the set at 7:30, and we worked about a week on that film.

Now, there was I -- as you know, in films the band were set up and you didn't see all the musicians. Some were behind posts and there was I being in the saxophone section, the tenor man, on the end and you couldn't see my face at all, my body, but you could see my foot and my dad said, 'You see that foot, that's my son's foot.'
